data.name: Anshumat
data.gender_notes: Anshumat is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anshumat is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'anshu', which means 'desire'. The name Anshumat is believed to refer to the god of peace and prosperity, Lord Anshuman. According to Hindu mythology, Lord Anshuman is the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. He is often depicted holding a trishula (a three-pronged weapon) and is believed to bestow peace, happiness, and prosperity upon his devotees.
data.etymology: Anshumat belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Peace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anshumat total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Anshumat was an ancient Vedic deity, considered to be a variant of Indra, the king of gods in Hindu mythology. He is mentioned in the Rigveda, the oldest known Hindu scriptures, in hymns dedicated to him.
Anshumat is also referred to in the Mahabharata, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, as the father of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty.
